sections.heading: Where we stand going into the final meeting (decided)

points.text: We are building a universal remote for young consumers (under forty), not a TV-only one for everybody.

citations.contains: we should go for universal
the younger people were defined under forty

points.text: Case: rubber, in the company's yellow, with the leaner shape (square base, rounded top) Mark chose in meeting c. It runs on regular batteries.

citations.contains: we're definitely going for rubber
take yellow
Okay, will just take regular batteries.

points.text: Interface: the deluxe edition with an LCD screen, no scroll wheel (voted out), and a beep plus flash so a lost remote can be found.

citations.contains: going towards the deluxe edition
No r no scroll-wheel
it goes beep and that you that some light lights up

points.text: Inside: the advanced chip (the LCD screen needs it) and rubber push-buttons, because a rubber case only takes rubber buttons.

citations.contains: The chip is advanced because we have the advanced features
we can only use rubber buttons

points.text: Targets from the kick-off still apply: selling price 25 Euros, production cost about 12.50 Euros.

citations.contains: Selling price, twenty five Euros

points.text: LCD screen: dropped in meeting b as too big, power-hungry and costly, then brought back in meeting c because users want it (deluxe edition).

citations.contains: we should lose the L_C_D_ screen
that seems to be what the people want

points.text: Speech recognition: ruled out by Mark in meeting b (too hard across countries and languages), reopened in meeting c once a small speech component turned up and Dirk reported that over sixty percent of target users want it. By the end of meeting c it was drawn into the design (microphone next to the transmitter) but never explicitly confirmed, and it has not been costed.

citations.contains: implementing speech recognition is such a small
So we can implement it
where do we want the microphone

points.text: Power: the rechargeable unit and charging base discussed in meeting b gave way to a normal battery in meeting c.

citations.contains: this rules out our unit our rechargeable unit
Okay, will just take regular batteries.

points.text: Changeable covers: welcomed in meeting b, then pushed out of the basic design to 'maybe later'; wood was ruled out at the same time.

citations.contains: let's just rule out wood for now
not something we're working with in the basic design

points.text: Nick (B, user interface) and Xavier (C, industrial design): work out the final design together, inside and outside, and bring the drawing to the meeting.

citations.contains: you should work together on the final design
doodle us a nice nice design for for the next meeting

points.text: Dirk (D, marketing): look up the exact survey figure on voice-recognition interest, do the market analysis, and find out what people are willing to pay above 25 Euros.

citations.contains: I'm I have to look it up
you're gonna do the market market uh analysing
you can find out i what people are willing to pay

points.text: Xavier (C, industrial design): still owes cost figures (none found yet, only that the LCD needs the more expensive advanced chip), and whether the remote can open the TV's own menu.

citations.contains: I still don't have any finance information
we need ano uh an advanced chip in it
we need to put some research into that if if we can open the menu

points.text: Mark (A, project manager): the final project report.

citations.contains: I'm supposed to do the little work on the year-end report

points.text: Budget risk: nobody has costed the design. Nick warned in meeting b that with an LCD the remote cannot sell for 25 Euros; the LCD forces the more expensive advanced chip and speech recognition adds its own component. Expect to cut something once the cost sheet arrives.

citations.contains: we're not going to be able to sell it for twenty-five then
too bad we don't have the finance

points.text: Speech recognition: confirm whether it stays once the costs are known, and if it does, whether the remote should also talk back (Xavier raised it, Nick doubted it is needed).

citations.contains: do you actually need the remote talking back

points.text: Shape: the working shape is Nick's design with the top rounded off, as Mark asked (it 'looks leaner'). Still open is the cost: Nick said smoothing the edges adds expense, and more curves cost more. Mark's wish for a rounder, fruit-like form was left to the covers, because Nick warned it follows one seasonal trend.

citations.contains: I tend to disagree with with uh with a sharp form
that's just for one seasonal trend
smooth the edges indeed. But that will bring extra
